newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Cash-strapped Russian airlines cut plane purchases.
newsitem.headline: Cash-strapped Russian airlines cut plane purchases.

text.p: Cash-strapped Russian airlines bought only four Russian-made aircraft between January and September of this year compared with 22 planes in the same period of 1995, a senior aviation official said on Tuesday.

Eduard Neimark, head of the aviation industry department of the defence industry ministry, told Reuters airlines did not have money to buy new aircraft. He said Russian carriers had planned to buy 80 planes during this year.
In 1992 they bought 83 passenger and cargo aircraft, he added.
"Forecasts show that Russian civil airlines will need 138 new aircraft for 1997," Neimark said.
He said the critical situation could be improved if a system for leasing aircraft were set up in Russia.
"But the economy ministry does not have the money for this," he said, adding that the Russian aviation industry needed urgent financial help from the state.
Neimark said, five leading plants in Ulyanovsk, Voronez, Saratov, Kazan and Samara were almost at a standstill.
He said Russian carriers would need to replace 1,600 aircraft by 2000.
Aeroflot said last month it wanted to buy 10 Boeing 737-400 jets to replace outdated Russian-built Tupolev-134 aircraft.
